title: Count exact nonzero carries for every reduced rational shear (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Prove the exact per-input carry count for every nonzero reduced rational shear `x <- x + (a/h)y`, with canonical low digits in `{0,...,q-1}` and `gcd(h,q)=1`.

```text
A = |a|, H = max(A,h), m = floor((q-1)/H)
zero exact carries Z = (m+1)q - A*m*(m+1)/2
nonzero exact carries = q^2-Z
```

Claim type: scoped written mathematical proof with finite corroboration. Both signs have the same count. At `q>=|a|+h`, the count also gives nonidentity high translations at every width `w>=2`. The package gives the separate exact prime-field `GL_n` conditioning law and a small-radix cancellation counterexample.

The limiting nonzero-carry proportions for coefficients `1`, `1/2` and `1/4` are `1/2`, `5/8` and `25/32`. More generally, the proportion for `1/2^s` increases to one. Smaller coefficients alone therefore do not imply fewer carry events.

This extends the per-input zero-correction boundary explicitly left outside Ali Romman's #5841 potential-site count. Credit #5841, Nick Petalas's earlier elementary carry identity, ToikY #5801/#5805, Tekalign #3343/#4000, JoyboyBrian and the retained G20/native/ROW lineage. Their source documents remain unchanged; no predecessor mathematical verifier is imported or replayed. Classical arithmetic-progression and general-linear-group row counting retain their credit. The new contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Apache-2.0.

[Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19216892). Canonical main remains `de5ec2e7a6074068452f45b1a191b5c72832df4a`, priority revision 8. The helper-contract card is explicitly changed to this carry-sparsity side result.

## Evidence

Before, #5841 allows input-dependent zero corrections without counting them. After, the written proof gives the closed form, sign symmetry, exact/high-residue distinction and invertible-matrix law.

Local CPython 3.12.15 on macOS arm64 passes:

- Warning-strict normal and isolated optimized direct checks, timed separately at 0.42s and 0.31s. Both print `PASS_RATIONAL_SHEAR_CARRY_DENSITY` with generated receipts binding all eight package files.
- 3,848 scalar fixtures and all 1,353,470 low pairs; 1,188 full-width fixtures and 168,044 low pairs against a direct full-modulus oracle; 14,176 arbitrary-high input cases.
- All 23,318 matrices in the six complete small domains, including 13,950 invertible matrices and 104 coefficient/domain combinations. These are GL2 at primes 2,3,5,7 and GL3 at primes 2,3.
- Five limiting fixtures, sixteen dyadic monotonicity cases, thirteen invalid-input rejections, three semantic separating controls and the small-radix cancellation control.
- Both registered VERIFY commands, metadata/provenance validation, AST parsing, in-memory compilation and staged whitespace checks.
- Exact committed bytes and declared-source ancestry at `91900a57a9378586d02cf2c3609873175441d558`; official package export/integrity; a read-only, empty-PATH, Git-free optimized export replay; deliberate retained-source corruption rejection.

Exact reproduction from the repository root:


An equivalent CPython 3.12 path works. Only the standard library is required. Pending source documents are retained with original head/blob/SHA256 records; replay needs no unmerged predecessor Git objects.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The main count concerns exact rational carries. Its high-translation interpretation has the stated sufficient radix bound and excludes width one. The GL law assumes a uniform complete general linear group over a prime field, not an arbitrary selected admissible subset or execution distribution. One-shear marginals do not determine correlated fused-route counts.

No physical predicate, low-cache preparation/erasure, carry-skipping program, amortization contract, total tape bill or actual G20 caller distribution is supplied. Uniform frequencies do not by themselves reduce a worst-case recursive invoice. Source native/tape suites, the selected cold replay and a formal proof-kernel run are unrun. All five framework assumptions retain their status. No new kappa, selected-frontier change, supplier admission or complete multiplication theorem is claimed. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Open next questions

1. Can one legal zero-carry branch beat unconditional translation after its predicate and full cache lifecycle are paid? Start with a released quarter-shear leaf and the literal tape interface; the branch and amortization contract are missing.
2. What is the joint zero-carry count for one complete fused route? Start with one exact two-coordinate restriction from #5841; coordinate correlation prevents multiplying these scalar marginals.

## Related open work

- #5841 supplies fused G20 carry algebra and potential sites; this result counts actual zero/nonzero events for a single elementary shear.
- #5849 implements a rotation from a supplied quarter-carry packet; this result does not implement its missing producer or change its physical bounds.
- #5846 supplies paid rational-coefficient preparation and shear leaves; the new count supplies no replacement leaf or tariff.
- #5842 installs affine-shear output in its original owner; this result concerns the correction coefficient before that execution interface.
- #5820 constructs sparse G20 port bases; this theorem neither resynthesizes nor physically realizes its routes.
- #5801 constructs dyadic normalizer words; this theorem counts scalar carry events without changing those words.
- #5805 binds actual markers to ROW words; this result supplies no cache/carry/commit implementation or physical marker binding.
- #5834 installs a shorter complete global G20 caller while retaining carry obligations; its endpoint and invoice are not recomputed here.
- #5840 simplifies G20 boundary words while retaining cache/carry obligations; this result gives no new bank-exchange synthesis or complete caller bill.
- #5913 counts distinguishable response functions for a serialized rational-shear packet producer; this result counts low input pairs with a nonzero correction, a different quantity.
- #5912 classifies retained history for nearest-even rounded shears; this theorem uses exact modular arithmetic and computes none of its history costs.

The completion refresh inspected the nine other open account PRs created since the CLAIM: #5909 through #5914 and #5916 through #5918. The same-object entries are #5912 and #5913, already distinguished above. The remaining submissions concern partition fees, batching, sector workspace, cyclic quotients, tensor phase recovery, tree degree and XOR synthesis. None computes the same carry-frequency quantity; no additional computations were run to compare their results.
